name: MAX1873SEEE+T
title: Current-limited switch-mode charger controller for 2-, 3- and 4-cell Li+ packs
summary: The MAX1873R, S and T control a buck converter with an external P-channel MOSFET to charge 2, 3 or 4 series Li+ cells with a regulated voltage (±0.75%) and current. A third loop limits current drawn from the adapter by reducing charge current, and IOUT reports charge current as a voltage. With the voltage loop disabled the part becomes a current source for NiCd or NiMH packs. Input up to 28 V, 300 kHz, 16-pin QSOP.
key_figures: 4.2 V per cell nominal; 8.4 V (R), 12.6 V (S), 16.8 V (T); adjustable ±5.25%

pins.name: CSSN
pins.function: Negative side of the input-current sense resistor. A resistor from CSSP to CSSN sets the limit on total current taken from the source; tying CSSN to CSSP turns input-current sensing off.

pins.name: CSSP
pins.function: Positive side of the input-current sense resistor; the pin is also the sense point for source undervoltage.

pins.name: CCS
pins.function: Compensation node of the input-source current loop.

pins.name: CCV
pins.function: Compensation node of the battery-voltage loop. A 1.5 kΩ pull-up to VL switches the voltage loop off, for NiCd or NiMH charging.

pins.name: CCI
pins.function: Compensation node of the charge-current loop.

pins.name: ICHG/EN
pins.function: Charge-current adjust and shutdown. A divider from REF to GND scales the CSB-BATT current-sense threshold, which is 200 mV with the pin tied to REF. Below 500 mV charging stops and supply current falls to 5 µA.

pins.name: IOUT
pins.function: Charge-current monitor: a voltage of 20 × (VCSB - VBATT), so 4 V at 200 mV of sense voltage. Load capacitance 5 nF at most.

pins.name: VADJ
pins.function: Battery regulation voltage adjust, from 3.979 V to 4.421 V per cell. Equal divider resistors (nominally 100 kΩ each) give 4.2 V per cell; with 1% resistors accuracy stays within 0.75%, because the span is narrow.

pins.name: REF
pins.function: 4.2 V reference output; needs a 1 µF ceramic capacitor to GND.

pins.name: BATT
pins.function: Battery voltage sense and negative side of the charge-current sense resistor. Capacitor to GND: 68 µF for the MAX1873R, 47 µF for the S, 33 µF for the T, with ESR under 1 Ω.

pins.name: CSB
pins.function: Positive side of the charge-current sense resistor.

pins.name: VH
pins.function: Internal regulator that feeds the EXT gate driver; a 0.22 µF ceramic capacitor goes from VH to DCIN.

pins.name: EXT
pins.function: Gate drive for the external P-channel MOSFET, swinging between VDCIN and VDCIN - 5 V.

pins.name: DCIN
pins.function: Supply input of the controller; 0.22 µF ceramic capacitor to GND.

pins.name: VL
pins.function: Internal 5.4 V regulator for the control logic; 2.2 µF or more of ceramic capacitance to GND.

circuits.title: Typical application circuit (Figure 1)
circuits.description: A step-down charger for a 2- to 4-cell Li+ pack that also feeds a system load. D1 takes the adapter input onto DCIN. RCSS (0.033 Ω) measures the total drawn from the adapter, filtered into CSSP and CSSN by RP/CP and RN/CN. Q1, D2 and L1 form the buck stage driven from EXT at 300 kHz; RCSB (0.068 Ω) sets about 3 A of charge current and its voltage drives IOUT. R1 and R2 from REF set VADJ and so the per-cell voltage. R3 holds ICHG/EN at REF; the DISABLE switch Q2 grounds it to stop charging. CCC, CCCS and the CCCVS-RCCV-CCCVP network compensate the three loops.

circuits.title: Typical operating circuit
circuits.description: A buck charger: input diode to DCIN, input-current sense resistor with RC filters into CSSP and CSSN, P-channel switch on EXT with catch diode and inductor, charge-current sense resistor from CSB to BATT, the VADJ divider from REF, and a series capacitor-resistor from CCV to GND beside a lone capacitor. ICHG/EN is tied straight to REF, so the charge current runs at full scale with no shutdown control.

operation.text: A buck converter built round an external P-channel MOSFET, inductor and diode charges 2, 3 or 4 Li+ cells in series. Three loops act on it: battery voltage (sensed at BATT), charge current (sensed across RCSB from CSB to BATT) and input current (sensed across RCSS). The default per-cell limit is 4.2 V, giving 8.4 V on the R, 12.6 V on the S and 16.8 V on the T.

The battery voltage is held within ±0.75%. VADJ, set between GND and REF, trims the per-cell voltage by ±5.25% about 4.2 V; because the span is small, 1% divider resistors still give the ±0.75% overall figure. Its compensation node is CCV, kept apart from the current loops; the network of the typical application circuit suits most designs.

Charge current is the voltage across RCSB over the 200 mV threshold (ICHG = 0.2 V / RCSB with ICHG/EN at REF); a lower ICHG/EN voltage scales it down. The current amplifier is compensated at CCI; 47 nF to GND suits most uses.

When current drawn from the adapter reaches the RCSS limit, charging current is cut back so the system load keeps its supply. The adapter then needs to cover only the input limit, not maximum system load plus maximum charge current. Connecting CSSP to CSSN bypasses the function. The loop is compensated at CCS, typically 47 nF to GND.

The MOSFET is switched at a fixed 300 kHz. Whichever of the CCI, CCV and CCS signals is lowest controls the duty cycle; the other two are clamped to within 200 mV of it so control passes between loops without delay. Dropout is 200 mV and duty cycle can reach 100%.

Pulling ICHG/EN below 0.5 V stops charging. The part also shuts down when DCIN falls below BATT. While shut down, the BATT divider inside is switched out, and the battery supplies about 1.5 µA with the adapter absent or the part shut down.
DCIN is compared with BATT; the charger turns off once DCIN drops below BATT + 50 mV, so an absent or low source does not drain the battery.
A diode usually feeds the charger from the source. It stops the battery discharging through the MOSFET body diode if the input is shorted, and guards against reversed or negative adapter voltages.
Below the BATT undervoltage threshold (5.0 V R, 7.5 V S, 10 V T typical) charge current is cut to ICHG/20. Below 2.5 V per cell the CSB-BATT sense voltage is regulated to 10 mV typical.
IOUT gives 20 times the CSB-BATT voltage, so a microcontroller ADC can use it for gas gauging, state of charge or time remaining. It drives up to 5 nF.

Per-cell voltage depends on the cell chemistry and build and comes from the battery maker. For 4.2 V per cell use two equal 100 kΩ resistors from REF to GND with the tap on VADJ; for other voltages compute VVADJ, choose R1 so the divider totals about 200 kΩ, then compute R2.
More inductance lowers ripple, but at a fixed size brings more series resistance and less saturation current. Ripple of about 30% to 50% of the average charge current is a good compromise.

Choose the P-channel MOSFET for efficiency, dissipation and temperature. On-resistance and gate charge set its loss and generally trade against each other. Conduction loss peaks at the lowest source voltage and highest battery voltage.
A Schottky from the MOSFET drain to GND, rated for at least the charge-current limit and for a reverse voltage above the highest input voltage.

It carries the switching current so it does not flow back through the adapter, and must handle the input RMS current. Its impedance matters for keeping AC current out of the adapter and for EMI limits. Low-ESR aluminium electrolytics work; tantalum or large ceramics usually do better.
It takes the inductor ripple, so its impedance must be well below the battery's. Both capacitance and ESR set filtering and PWM loop stability.

The input-current, charge-current and voltage loops are compensated at CCS, CCI and CCV. 47 nF from CCI and from CCS to GND covers most chargers; larger values narrow those loops' bandwidth. At CCV, a series RC to GND sits beside a lone capacitor to GND; the typical application circuit gives values.

Two internal linear regulators run the part: VL for the control circuits and VH for the gate drive. VL can feed a little external circuitry up to 3 mA. Required low-ESR ceramics: 2.2 µF VL to GND, 0.22 µF VH to DCIN, 1 µF REF to GND, for stability.

A 1.5 kΩ pull-up from CCV to VL disables the voltage loop, leaving the part a current source; the battery undervoltage features still reduce current at low VBATT. The R suits 5 or 6 Ni cells, the S 7 to 9, the T 10. There is no Ni termination: an external microcontroller or Ni charge controller must end the charge.
BiCMOS process, 1397 transistors.
